title: Home
text: Boone Bowles Assistant Professor of Finance Adam C. Sinn '00 Department of Finance Mays Business School | Texas A&M University boone.bowles@tamu.edu | Curriculum Vitae I research asset pricing and institutional investors, with projects on stock-market anomalies, mutual funds, short selling, information acquisition, and financial social media. I teach corporate finance in the Full-Time MBA, Anthony Bahr ’91 Engineering MBA, and Flex-Online MBA programs. I also created Boone’s Finance Boot Camp , a free, self-paced finance curriculum. I earned my Ph.D. in finance at the University of North Carolina and my M.S. in financial economics and B.S. in economics at Utah State University. I like to exercise, read, and be with my wife and children.

title: Boot Camp
text: Boone’s Finance Boot Camp A free, self-paced resource for students preparing for a finance course or reviewing a particular concept. It covers time value of money, bonds, financial statements, free cash flow, and valuation. Open Boone’s Finance Boot Camp The Project I created the Boot Camp to help students review foundational material outside class, leaving more class time for application and feedback. It brings together 19 videos, seven practice banks with 1,400 questions, notes, six Excel workbooks, a financial calculator, and VB—Virtual Boone, a tutor grounded in the course materials. Students can follow the sequence or return to a specific explanation, practice bank, or workbook. Practice questions provide immediate feedback and links to relevant lessons. Faculty can link directly to the materials that fit their courses. Project Report (PDF, 6 pages) | Project Poster (PDF) Prepared for the Montague–Center for Teaching Excellence Scholar Award, September 2026. What I Learned Building the Boot Camp changed how I think about producing teaching materials. AI made it easier to turn my existing explanations and examples into videos, notes, practice questions, and tools. I still had to decide what students needed to learn, choose the sequence, and review the finance. Keeping the materials organized together also made it easier to carry a correction or a new example across them. The project also sharpened a distinction for me: helping students practice and assessing what they have learned require different evidence. Quiz attempts and feedback can help me improve the resource, but they do not by themselves establish individual mastery or learning gains. Acknowledgment The Boot Camp was made possible by support from the Montague family and the Texas A&M Center for Teaching Excellence through the Montague–Center for Teaching Excellence Scholar Award. I am grateful for the opportunity to develop this resource for students and faculty.
